data.heading: What to expect on your first Sunday
data.body:
Visiting a church for the first time can feel a little daunting. Here's what to expect when you visit [Church Name].

When you arrive, someone from our welcome team will say hello. They can show you where to sit, where the restrooms are and where the children's program meets.

The service lasts about [X] minutes. [Describe the main parts, such as songs, prayer, a reading and a sermon.] You're welcome to join in as much or as little as you like. Nobody will put you on the spot.

Come as you are. There's no dress code, and nobody expects you to know what to do or when to stand.

If you have children, they're welcome to stay with you or join our children's program, where trained volunteers will look after them. [Edit to match your program.]

Afterwards, stay for coffee if you can. It's a good time to meet people and ask questions.

If you'd like to know more before you visit, send us a message. We'd be glad to hear from you.

data.heading: Finding your place: small groups and serving
data.body:
Sunday worship is just one part of church life. Many people find that the friendships really grow during the week.

Small groups are a simple way to start. A handful of people meet in a home or at church to talk, pray and support each other. Groups are relaxed, and you don't need to know anything in advance.

Serving is another way to connect. Helping on the welcome team, at a community meal or with the children's program lets you meet people while doing something useful.

There's no pressure to do everything. Start with one thing that interests you and see how it goes. If it isn't the right fit, we'll help you find something else.

Not sure where to begin? Fill in the form on our Get involved page or talk to anyone on the welcome team after the service. We'd love to help you find your place at [Church Name].
